# nosms — full manual (llms-full.txt)

This is the expandable companion to `llms.txt`. `llms.txt` is the contract;
this file is the manual. Both are served by the CVM server (`docs` and
`llms-full` tools) and bundled into the napplet at build time so a human or an
agent can read them offline.

## 1. What the service is

nosms sends one SMS to one phone number on behalf of a nostr key. There is no
account, no API key and no signup: your nostr key is your identity and you pay
per message in sats, postage-style. The v1 rail is a single personal
JMP/Cheogram line, so treat volume limits as real.

## 2. Two surfaces, one transport contract

| Surface | Who uses it | How |
|---|---|---|
| ContextVM (MCP over Nostr, kind `25910`) | agents, in-shell clients | call the tools by server npub |
| HTTP (`https://nosms.orangesync.tech`) | scripts, `curl`, LLMs with network access | NIP-98-authenticated `POST /api/send` |

Both sit on the same `Transport` interface and the same price table. A napplet
cannot use the HTTP surface: `NAP-RESOURCE` is bytes-in/bytes-out with no HTTP
verb, so a `POST` with a body is not expressible from a sandboxed napplet. That
is exactly why the napplet wraps the CVM.

## 3. Tools

### `sms.send(to, body)` — PAID

- `to` — E.164 destination (`+141****4652`). Formatting is stripped; a string
  with no digits is `bad_destination`.
- `body` — the message text.

Never sends before payment lands (`explicit_gating`). The shell answers the
CEP-8 `payment_required` notification and pays; a payment refusal is reported as
`payment denied` and nothing is dispatched.

Result fields:

- `id` — the send record id, used with `sms.status`.
- `accepted` — `true` when the rail accepted the message for dispatch.
- `rail` — the rail name that accepted it.
- `best_effort` — echoed from the rail's own capability flags.

### `sms.status(id)` — free

Returns the stored send record: destination, price paid, rail, acceptance and
any refund. It never claims delivery on a rail that cannot observe it.

### `sms.pricing` — free

The live flat price in sats. Returns `unit: "sats"`, `model: "flat"`, the price,
and the ADR-0002 formula inputs (`risk_multiplier`, `rail_replacement_usd`).

The price does not depend on the destination: the v1 rail's plan is unlimited
including international, so a per-country price would advertise a distinction the
rail does not have. A destination is still validated (a string with no digits is
`bad_destination`), and the price is never zero — an unrecognised destination
takes the documented default rather than becoming free.

### `sms.capabilities` — free

The rail name and its capability flags, read from the rail itself:

- `best_effort` — `true` means there is no retry guarantee.
- `delivery_receipts` — `false` means NO delivery confirmation is possible.
- `countries` — destinations the rail will attempt.

### `docs` (alias `llms`) — free

Returns the `llms.txt` contract verbatim. Callers must not need out-of-band
knowledge: everything required to use the service is reachable from the server.

### `llms-full` — free

Returns this manual.

## 4. Payment (CEP-8)

- Gating: `explicit_gating`.
- Capability tags: `cap:tool:sms.send:2900:sats` — one flat price, one tool.
  ADR-0002 supersedes the earlier per-destination caps; the free tools
  (`sms.status`, `sms.pricing`, `sms.capabilities`, `docs`) carry no `cap`,
  because a price on a free call would claim money is required for it.
- PMI: `bitcoin-cashu` (primary). A Lightning PMI may be added later.
- Refunds: a hard failure the rail can detect is refunded automatically. A
  `best_effort` miss — the rail accepted and the carrier silently dropped the
  message — is NOT refundable, because the rail cannot see it.
- Owner allowlist: the operator's own npub sends free; paying yourself is
  pointless. Every other caller pays.

## 5. Error contract

ContextVM errors arrive in the envelope `error` field:
`payment required`, `payment denied`, `policy denied`, `unsupported method`,
`server not found`, `relay timeout`.

The HTTP surface carries the same vocabulary as headers:

- `X-Reason`: `insufficient_funds`, `bad_destination`, `rail_not_configured`,
  `transport_error`, `rate_limited`, `owner_only`, `auth_missing`,
  `auth_invalid`, `auth_expired`, `auth_replayed`, `auth_url_mismatch`,
  `auth_method_mismatch`, `auth_payload_mismatch`, `invalid_request`,
  `not_found`, `method_not_allowed`, `internal_error`.
- `X-Hint`: one human-readable sentence.

## 6. Honest limits (read before building on this)

1. **No delivery receipts.** `sms.send` returning `accepted: true` means the
   rail took the message. It does not mean the handset received it. Do not
   build OTP confirmation, escrow release on delivery, or any
   delivery-dependent logic on this rail.
2. **Best effort.** No retry guarantee.
3. **One personal line.** Throughput is that of a single phone number.
4. **Countries.** The rail reports what it will attempt; it does not guarantee
   coverage.

## 7. Data handling

Destination numbers and message bodies are retained only for status lookups and
refunds. No marketing use, no third-party sharing, no analytics. Message bodies
on the HTTP surface are NIP-44-encrypted client-to-gateway and are never stored
in plaintext at the service.

## 8. Running the napplet

The napplet requires exactly one shell capability: `cvm`. Everything else —
theme, storage, notify — is optional and feature-detected. It never holds a key
and never holds an ecash token: payment runs through the shell's CEP-8 flow.

---
*Manual version: v1 draft. The authoritative values are always the live
`sms.pricing` and `sms.capabilities` responses.*
